motivo: A normal day: ChatGPT-IA-edu with Microsoft Classroom and the English regulator's warning on assessment; Vibe Coding Educativo with two classroom resources and a debate about interfaces; EduMedia-IAG, quiet, with the Unreal Engine 5.9 preview.

piezas.titular: Microsoft unveils Classroom, a dedicated space to centre classwork on Microsoft 365
piezas.entradilla: Microsoft Classroom brings assignments, grades and AI tools together on a single screen for primary, secondary and higher education. It arrives in 2027 at no extra cost for schools on certain plans.
cuerpo: Microsoft has announced Microsoft Classroom on its [education blog](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/educationblog/introducing-microsoft-classroom-a-new-experience-built-for-teaching-and-learning/4571185), a standalone Microsoft 365 Education experience for teaching and learning. The company describes it as a “front door” to tools that teachers already know, and makes clear that it does not replace Teams for Education.

It brings assignments, classwork, grades, the OneNote Class Notebook, Learning Accelerators and analytics tools together in one place. On logging in, teachers see the work waiting to be marked and what is due that week; students see what is coming up, what is overdue and what has been returned with comments. Each class also has a shared home page that the teacher can customise. It will be used on the web, and there will be mobile and desktop apps.
It includes AI features: Teach, the AI planning space for teachers, a study and learning agent that can be used within assignments, and learning activities for students.

According to Microsoft, it will be included at no additional cost in the A1, A3, A5 and A7 plans from 2027, and in A2 and above in future products from January 2028. A preview is planned for early 2027, which school administrators can sign up for.

fuentes.titulo: Introducing Microsoft Classroom: a new experience built for teaching and learning (Microsoft Community Hub)

piezas.comprobado: Re-read the official announcement on Microsoft's education blog: standalone experience, does not replace Teams, features, AI features (Teach, study and learning agent, activities), web and apps, plans (A1, A3, A5, A7 in 2027; A2 and above in future products from January 2028) and a preview in early 2027. Telegram message confirmed. Does not contradict anything in publicado.txt.

piezas.titular: England's university regulator calls for more assessment without AI and reopens the debate on how to verify authorship
piezas.entradilla: The Office for Students recommends secure formats such as in-person or oral exams. In the group, members debated what can and cannot be detected.
cuerpo: The Office for Students (OfS), the higher education regulator in England, published its [page on artificial intelligence in higher education](https://www.officeforstudents.org.uk/for-providers/quality-and-standards/artificial-intelligence-in-higher-education/) on 11 November, drawing on work done with Advance HE. The report, [Making AI work for students](https://www.officeforstudents.org.uk/publications/making-ai-work-for-students-reflections-on-institutional-practice/), warns that many unsupervised tasks can now be completed with AI to a high standard and with little involvement from the student, and calls for assessments to measure what students know and can do, often through secure, AI-free formats: in-person exams, presentations, oral exams and practical tasks. It acknowledges that these formats have costs and may disadvantage some disabled students, and it also describes assessments in which AI use is permitted or required.

The news led the group into a deeper discussion. One view holds that short online courses have lost their point, because an assistant with a browser extension can complete them on its own. Another recalls that, as mentioned in the group, there are Moodle plug-ins that try to detect AI from the speed or regularity of answers, but that there are also extensions that write like a person and prompts that make text undetectable. From there two conclusions emerge that sit side by side: that accusing someone of using AI is not the way forward, and that, in an electronic environment, any parameter of what is human can be imitated if a person can do it.

The report does not consider detectors reliable either: it is difficult to establish conclusively whether AI was used, and a detector's output should be, at most, one more piece of evidence, with suspicion never lowering a grade. The paper has already covered the debate on [detectors and the “witch hunt”](pieza:2026-11-01/detectores-caza-brujas) and how [a detector percentage does not prove copying](pieza:2026-11-08/detector-ia-no-es-prueba).

fuentes.titulo: Artificial intelligence in higher education (Office for Students)
Making AI work for students: reflections on institutional practice (Office for Students and Advance HE)

piezas.comprobado: Opened the OfS page (project with Advance HE, 11 November date tied to the press release; it says nothing specific about assessment or detectors) and the Unite.AI article, which is the source of the secure formats, costs, disability, not removing AI and the point about detectors, all attributed to it. The views on online courses, Moodle plug-ins and extensions come from the thread and have not been verified elsewhere (now stated in the text). Pieza keys: from publicado.txt, both exist and deal with detectors. Telegram message confirmed.

piezas.titular: Relleu Obert turns a piece of real map into a 3D model that can be printed for the classroom
piezas.entradilla: A free, open-source project lets you pick a place, generate its relief in the browser and export it for 3D printing.
cuerpo: [Relleu Obert](https://relleu.ortogra.fi/), with the slogan “Geografia que pots tocar” (“Geography you can touch”), generates 3D models of real places that can be viewed in the browser and printed. According to its website, it is the work of Aarón Fortuño, it is free and open source under the MIT licence, and for now the interface is available only in Catalan, with four other languages still to come.

You start from an address or coordinates and choose the size, whether you want just the relief or the full model, and the vertical exaggeration. You can add trees, rivers, roads, paths and buildings drawn from OpenStreetMap, the Institut Cartogràfic i Geològic de Catalunya (ICGC) and the Cadastre, draw routes or import a GPX file, and leave holes for pins or flags. The models are exported as 3MF or STL.

The author says in the group that he built it with AI and that the mesh is calculated in the browser, with no data stored on a server. His motivation is that, when working on relief with primary school pupils, paper means little to them and being able to touch the model enriches the experience. He shares photos of the first prototype printed at his school, a 10 × 10 cm model of a cove with cliffs, and announces a separate repository of models of notable places in more detail.

fuentes.titulo: Relleu Obert — Geografia que pots tocar (in Catalan)

piezas.comprobado: Opened the Relleu Obert website: features, data (OSM, ICGC, Cadastre), GPX, holes for pins, STL/3MF, MIT licence and authorship; only Catalan is active (the other four languages are listed as pending, although the group message treats them as available). Removed “one file per material”, not confirmed for 3MF. The use of AI, the prototype, the motivation and the model repository are what the author says in the group. Telegram message confirmed.

piezas.titular: A Catalan-language website tells the story of the spice trade from Marco Polo onwards with maps, games and questions
piezas.entradilla: “El comerç de les espècies” offers nine interactive chapters, designed, according to its author, for secondary school and sixth-form students.
cuerpo: [El comerç de les espècies](https://ja.cat/especies) (“The spice trade”), created according to the group by Felip Sarroca i Gil, starts from a question: why did such tiny seeds set ships, money and empires in motion? It runs from the voyages of Marco Polo to the present day in nine chapters, each with an infographic, maps and activities, and ends with a challenge in which students argue their own answer.

The site includes calculators, wind maps, a merchant game, questions with instant feedback, an easy-reading option and a glossary. Progress is saved only in the browser. The author says that, before designing it, he asked Codex to connect to NotebookLM via MCP to create a notebook, gather sources and generate materials.

fuentes.titulo: El comerç de les espècies (in Catalan)

piezas.comprobado: Opened the website (it redirects to felipsarroca.github.io/web/Especies/): nine chapters, infographic, maps and activities, final challenge, calculators, wind maps, merchant game, questions with instant feedback, easy reading, glossary and progress in the browser. The site names neither the author nor the level: both come from the group message (now stated as such). The use of Codex and NotebookLM is what the author says. Telegram message confirmed.

piezas.titular: Terminal or app: teachers compare ways of working with a coding agent
piezas.entradilla: The group discussed whether the terminal offers more freedom than the graphical app, and concluded that it depends on the person and the task.
cuerpo: A conversation among users of Claude and other coding agents set two ways of working against each other. Those who prefer the terminal describe it as direct communication with the AI, with no buttons or icons in between, and use it even to organise personal documents and maintain a memory system; they keep the web interface for quick queries, mostly from their phone.

Those who prefer the desktop app argue that it is the same thing with a graphical interface, that it starts in a second, allows several chats at once within a single project, organises shortcuts and makes it easier to connect external tools. They add that, when working by projects and chats, everything depends on the service's own memory. Someone pointed out that working with information in the cloud raises the question of privacy, and another person replied that their method keeps the documents on their own computer with encrypted backups.

There was agreement on the essentials: web, app and terminal are three routes to a similar result, and knowing how to choose the tool and the interface for each case is part of learning, something that some members of the group linked to AI literacy. It is an exchange of preferences and experiences, with no verifiable data.
piezas.comprobado: Cross-checked with the group's messages (#14873-#14944 and #14912-#14963): the views match and carry no names. Opinion piece with no claims about products, figures or rules. Telegram message opened: it belongs to the thread.

piezas.titular: Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview adds MCP so AI agents can create 3D environments
piezas.entradilla: Epic Games has released a preview version of the engine with AI features, all of them experimental.
cuerpo: In EduMedia-IAG, members shared the announcement of [Unreal Engine 5.9 MegaJam Preview](https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/unreal-engine-5-9-megajam-preview/2852840), published by Epic on 9 November ahead of its AI MegaJam. It is of interest to anyone creating educational games and 3D environments.

The release adds Unreal MCP, which lets an AI agent control the editor (creating levels, profiling, debugging), an “Unreal Assistant” panel for working inside the editor with an external agent such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode, and Unreal Canvas, a tool for generating images, 3D meshes and video using your own keys. Epic marks everything as experimental and warns of “rough edges”; it recommends trying it on a copy of the project.

fuentes.titulo: Unreal Engine 5.9 MegaJam Preview (Epic Games forums)

piezas.comprobado: Re-read Epic's official forum post: 9 November date, Unreal MCP, Unreal Assistant, Unreal Canvas with your own keys, experimental features, “rough edges” and the recommendation to use a copy; the MegaJam runs from 12 to 15 November. The link shared was to a video game news site and is not used. Telegram message confirmed.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A terminal labelled “Agent” and a cube labelled “3D editor” joined by a double-headed arrow labelled “MCP”; beneath the cube, a red zigzag line and the label “Experimental”.

breves.texto: Anthropic advises that, to keep Fable 5.2 responsible for an action, you should write “ask for approval before deleting files” instead of “never delete files”, and reply with the specific instruction rather than a simple “go ahead”. It follows [the guide the paper reported on](pieza:2026-11-11/prompt-propiedad-codigo-fable).
Claude Whiteboards and Sheets, in beta, and Claude Data, which replaces Dashboards, were announced on 10 November and are available on all paid plans.

The author of the [school music bell](pieza:2026-11-06/timbre-musical-escolar) has published their project on GitHub: an installation guide, a manual for the staff and the code, with an AGPL licence for the code and CC BY-SA 4.0 for the documentation.
